text: It was a bright, sunny morning at Gan West!
All the friends ran outside to the school garden, laughing and jumping.
Today was a very special day — it was Bug Hunter Day!
Cru, Mason, Shai, Desi, Mia Alma, Aila, Chaya, and Mia Alexandra were so excited they could hardly stand still!
Morah Sarah smiled at all the happy faces. "Are you ready to find some tiny creatures?" she asked.
Morah Sarah held up a tray full of colorful magnifying glasses.
"Every Bug Hunter needs one of these!" she said with a big smile.
The children reached out their small hands, each taking a magnifying glass.
Mia Alexandra held hers up and giggled. "Everything looks so BIG!"
"Your mission," said Morah Sarah, "is to find every tiny creature hiding in our garden!"
Mia Alma crept slowly through the tall green plants.
Suddenly she stopped and gasped. "Look! Look! Come and see!"
Cru and Aila tiptoed over to where Mia Alma was pointing.
There on a big green leaf was a fuzzy green caterpillar, munching away!
"It's so soft and wiggly," whispered Mia Alma, her blue eyes wide with wonder.
Teacher Elizabeth waved her hand gently. "Come here, friends. I want to show you something amazing."
Mason, Chaya, and Desi scurried over and looked up at a little branch.
Hanging from the branch was a tiny, teardrop-shaped cocoon.
"Inside that cocoon," said Teacher Elizabeth softly, "a caterpillar is turning into a butterfly."
"It's like magic," Chaya whispered, her mouth dropping open.
Cru, Shai, Mia Alexandra, and Mia Alma stopped in the middle of the garden.
Two exciting things caught their eyes at the very same moment!
Over on one side, a sparkly spider web glittered in the sunshine between two flowers.
And on the other side, a big mossy log sat quietly on the ground.
"Which one should we explore first?" said Shai. It was a very hard choice!
Aila knelt down very slowly and very carefully near the spider web.
The web stretched between two pretty flower stems, thin as a hair.
Right in the middle sat a tiny, tiny spider, working very hard.
"It's making the web all by itself!" Aila breathed in a tiny whisper.
The web sparkled in the sunlight like it was covered in little diamonds.
Mason and Desi found a big mossy log on the ground.
They looked at each other and smiled. "Should we peek underneath?"
Together they grabbed the edge of the log and gently, gently lifted it up.
A whole family of rolly pollies was hiding underneath — little gray bugs curling into tiny balls!
"They're rolling up! They're rolling up!" Desi squealed with delight.
All eight friends gathered together on the soft green grass.
Everyone had something amazing to share!
Aila talked about the spinning spider. Mason and Desi showed everyone how rolly pollies curl up.
Mia Alma described every fuzzy stripe on the caterpillar she had found.
"There are SO many creatures living right here in our garden!" said Mia Alexandra with big wide eyes.
Teacher Virginia smiled and clapped her hands. "Everyone, follow me! Something is happening!"
She led all eight friends back to the branch where the cocoon was hanging.
The cocoon was wiggling and shaking! Back and forth, back and forth.
Every single child held their breath and stood perfectly still.
"Something is waking up inside," Teacher Virginia whispered. "Watch very carefully."
Crack! The cocoon split open — just a little at first.
Then slowly, slowly, two beautiful wings began to push their way out.
The wings were bright orange and black — the most beautiful colors anyone had ever seen!
The butterfly opened its wings wider and wider, stretching them for the very first time.
"Ohhhhh," all the children breathed together in a great big happy sigh.
The butterfly fluttered up into the air above the children's heads.
Cru, Shai, Mason, and Mia Alexandra watched it dance in the breeze.
"We found so many amazing bugs today," said Mason. "How do we remember them all?"
Mia Alexandra had an idea. "We could count every single bug in the whole garden!"
Cru had another idea. "Or we could draw them in our nature journals!" What do you think they should do?
The friends burst out in all directions, running and searching through the whole garden!
Chaya found a caterpillar. "One!" she called out, holding up one finger.
Shai spotted a spider web. "Two!" he shouted, running over to look.
Then Mia Alma found a fat pink worm wiggling in the soil. "A worm! A worm! That's a surprise bug!"
By the time they were done, they had counted twelve whole bugs — more than all their fingers!
Teacher Jocelyn spread a big colorful blanket on the soft grass in the garden.
She handed every child a tiny nature journal and a box of crayons.
"Draw your very favorite bug from today," said Teacher Jocelyn with a warm smile.
Mia Alexandra drew a butterfly with big orange wings. Desi drew a fat round rolly polly.
The garden was quiet and peaceful as little tongues poked out in concentration.
The beautiful butterfly was still floating gently around the garden.
Chaya stood very still and slowly, slowly held out her finger.
The butterfly circled once, circled twice — and then landed softly on Chaya's finger!
Mia Alma, Aila, and Mason all gasped at exactly the same time.
Chaya did not move a muscle. She just smiled the biggest smile she had ever smiled in her whole life.
After all that exploring, everyone was very, very hungry.
Morah Sarah appeared with a tray and a twinkle in her eye. "I have a special snack for all our Bug Hunters!"
On the tray were pretzel spiders, gummy worms, and round cookie rolly pollies!
"We can EAT the bugs?!" said Shai, and everyone burst out laughing.
The friends sat together munching their bug snacks and talking about all the amazing things they had found.
The friends waved goodbye as the orange butterfly floated up, up, up into the big blue sky.
"See you next time!" called Mia Alma, waving both hands.
Later that afternoon, it was nap time at Gan West.
Eight little friends lay down on their soft mats and closed their tired eyes.
And as they drifted off to sleep, each one dreamed of caterpillars, rolly pollies, spiders, and a beautiful butterfly — the tiny creatures of Gan West.
